extensionAudit.reason: identity IS the path (source_ref_key); cannot represent a file independently of path by construction; adding an opaque id column here would still leave the row's own PK/uniqueness path-derived unless the table is restructured, which is functionally the same cost as a new table

this table's entire purpose is per-revision observation (one row per (repo, workspace_revision, path)); repurposing it to also carry logical identity would conflate PROJECTION_COORDINATE with CANONICAL_LOGICAL_ID, which the design gate explicitly forbids

shape is alias-of-a-path-string (canonical_source_ref is itself a path, not an opaque id); 0 live rows, DEAD_WRITER; could plausibly be EXTENDED for the StableFileAliasV1 MECHANISM (effective_from/effective_to + evidence + status columns are the right shape) once a stableFileId column is added to it, but cannot itself become the identity owner

has real transition_kind/old_key/new_key/old_revision/new_revision/reviewer_id/evidence_refs -- the best-shaped existing rename/move-decision mechanism found. BUT its entity_kind CHECK constraint (confirmed live: only 'test'/'schema_object') excludes 'file' and has no repo_id column at all. EXTEND_EXISTING_OWNER is plausible for the MECHANISM if a future migration widens the CHECK constraint and adds repo scoping, but it cannot be repurposed as-is.

confirmed live: repo_id is populated with exactly one value ('deeds-web-app') across every table that has the column; graphify_files has no repository column at all; no table anywhere maps the 6 known git submodules to a canonical identity
effective_from/effective_to columns exist on atlas_source_aliases (0/... populated) and atlas_source_refs (0/46945 populated per S01-08); no table has ever recorded a tombstone event

repositoryIdentityDesign.problem: S01-08 proved the root registry is effectively hardcoded to 'deeds-web-app' and the six nested repositories (git submodules, confirmed live this session from .gitmodules: claude-mem, granite-docling-258M, mcp-server-mcp, models/embeddinggemma_300m, sites/parent-atlas-gateboard, turbovec) have zero registry identity anywhere.
repositoryIdentityDesign.designPrinciple: Do not infer identity from directory nesting alone. Do not use source-count equality as namespace proof. A repository's identity comes from its own external coordinates (its .gitmodules path + its own independent commit history), not from where it happens to be checked out inside the parent tree.

contract.name: RepositoryIdentityV1

fields.repositoryId: UUIDv7, minted once by the canonical creator, never regenerated
fields.canonicalCoordinates: { gitmoduleName: text (the .gitmodules key, e.g. 'granite-docling-258M'), gitmodulePath: text (checkout path relative to the parent repo root), originUrl: text | null, knownCommitOids: text[] (append-only history of observed submodule commit SHAs -- NOT identity, just observation history) }
fields.repositoryRelativePathNamespace: every StableFileRevisionBindingV1 row's repositoryRelativePath is only unique WITHIN one repositoryId -- this is what makes 'CROSS-REPOSITORY SAME PATH -> distinct stableFileIds' hold structurally, not by convention
fields.parentRelationship: optional parentRepositoryId (nullable) -- e.g. models/embeddinggemma_300m nested inside deeds-web-app; recorded as observed fact, never used to infer or merge identity

contract.rootRepository: deeds-web-app itself gets its own RepositoryIdentityV1 row too -- it is not a privileged default, it is repository #0 with the same contract as the 6 submodules. This removes the 'hardcoded repo <-> deeds-web-app equivalence is not persisted proof' finding from S01-08 by making it an explicit, minted, checked row instead of an assumption baked into every other table's default.

stableFileContract.coreDistinction: stableFileId = logical file lifecycle identity. sourceRevision = content/revision identity. repositoryRelativePath = observation/binding, never identity. graphify file UUID (graphify_files.file_id) = occurrence/revision identity, not logical identity. treeNodeOccurrenceId (atlas_ast_nodes.tree_node_id) = declaration/AST occurrence identity, a fourth, separate axis (S01-09C). These four are never conflated.

StableFileRevisionBindingV1.workspaceRevision: text, sha256:<64hex> shape enforced (reuses the S01-10B REVISION_RE contract, not a new regex)

StableFileAliasV1.aliasPath: text (a PRIOR path this stableFileId was known at)
StableFileAliasV1.validToRevision: text | null (sha256 shape; null = still the most recent alias before the current path)
StableFileAliasV1.evidence: jsonb (what proved the rename -- e.g. a git rename-detection receipt, never inferred from path/content/treeNodeId/packetId/git-commit alone per the design gate's explicit prohibition)

stableFileContract.hardRule: stableFileId is assigned ONCE by exactly one canonical creator, on an explicit CREATE lifecycle event. It is NEVER a column default (DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() on a revision-row table would mint a new logical id per revision, exactly the graphify_files.file_id anti-pattern this design exists to fix).

schemaProposal.note: DESIGN ONLY. Not applied. No DDL executed. Prefers extending atlas_source_aliases's MECHANISM (effective_from/effective_to/evidence/status shape) for StableFileAliasV1 rather than inventing a fifth alias-shaped table, but StableFileIdentityV1/StableFileRevisionBindingV1/RepositoryIdentityV1 are new tables -- no existing table can safely absorb canonical logical identity per the extensionAudit above.

proposedTables.name: atlas_repository_identity
columns: created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
proposedTables.transactionOwner: a new, single canonical script (S01-08I) -- name TBD, e.g. mint-repository-identity-v1.mjs

proposedTables.name: atlas_stable_file_identity
columns: repository_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES atlas_repository_identity(repository_id)
lifecycle_state text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ACTIVE' CHECK (lifecycle_state IN ('ACTIVE','TOMBSTONED'))
created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
uniqueConstraints: PRIMARY KEY (stable_file_id) -- the ONLY uniqueness; explicitly NOT unique on any path
proposedTables.transactionOwner: the same single canonical creator as above (S01-08I) -- NEVER a column DEFAULT

proposedTables.name: atlas_stable_file_revision_binding
columns: observed_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
uniqueConstraints: UNIQUE (stable_file_id, workspace_revision) -- one binding per stable file per workspace snapshot; path uniqueness is intentionally scoped by (repository_id via stable_file_id join, workspace_revision, repository_relative_path), NEVER globally unique by path alone -- this is what makes PATH_REUSE_NEW_ID and CROSS-REPOSITORY-SAME-PATH hold
proposedTables.transactionOwner: the canonical creator (CREATE/MODIFY events) -- read/observation only for every other consumer

proposedTables.name: atlas_stable_file_alias
columns: repository_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES atlas_repository_identity(repository_id)
valid_to_revision text CHECK (valid_to_revision IS NULL OR valid_to_revision ~ '^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$')
proposedTables.transactionOwner: the canonical creator, RENAME lifecycle event only -- never inferred automatically

schemaProposal.tombstoneSemantics: lifecycle_state = 'TOMBSTONED' + tombstoned_at set; a tombstoned stableFileId is never reused, never re-activated, and a subsequent CREATE at the same path always mints a NEW stableFileId unless a separately-proven RENAME/continuity event says otherwise (per the design gate's explicit fail-closed rule)
schemaProposal.aliasSemantics: atlas_stable_file_alias rows are append-only; validToRevision null means 'this alias was valid up to the file's current/most-recent binding'; an alias is only ever written by the canonical creator on a proven RENAME event, never inferred from path/content/treeNodeId/packetId/graphify-file-uuid/git-commit similarity alone

canonicalCreator.entrypoint: one new script (name TBD at S01-08H/I, not written yet) -- e.g. scripts/atlas/mint-stable-file-identity-v1.mjs
canonicalCreator.transactionBoundary: one bounded transaction per lifecycle event (CREATE, MODIFY-binding, RENAME-alias, TOMBSTONE), never a bulk unscoped mint
canonicalCreator.conflictBehavior: CREATE is idempotent per (repository_id, first-observed source_identity_key) via an explicit dedup check BEFORE minting -- never ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on a UUIDv7 PK, since that would silently accept a duplicate identity for what should have been recognized as SAFE_EXISTING_CONTINUITY
canonicalCreator.readback: required after every mint -- reads its own just-written row back inside the same transaction before COMMIT, matching this gate's established S01-10E pattern
canonicalCreator.moveRenameAction: writes exactly one atlas_stable_file_alias row recording the OLD path with valid_to_revision = the revision the move was observed at, then writes/updates atlas_stable_file_revision_binding with the NEW path -- the stable_file_id itself never changes
canonicalCreator.deleteTombstoneAction: sets lifecycle_state = TOMBSTONED + tombstoned_at; no row is deleted (this repo's own archive-not-delete convention, applied to logical identity too)
canonicalCreator.samePathRecreateAction: MINTS A NEW stableFileId by default; only reuses the tombstoned one if a separately-proven continuity event exists (never inferred from path equality alone -- this is the design gate's explicit rule and this repo's existing Duplication Prevention discipline applied to identity)

writerOwnership.everyOtherWriter: PROJECTION or LEGACY, never a second creator: graphify_files (REVISION_RECORD_ID projection), atlas_packets.file_id (legacy duplicate namespace, do not extend), atlas_source_refs/atlas_workspace_source_bindings (path/revision projections that the canonical creator READS from to decide when to mint, but never writes stableFileId itself)
writerOwnership.hardRule: There must not be two stableFileId generators. Confirmed this census: zero existing writers mint anything resembling stableFileId today (S01-08's own finding, 'NO_PRODUCER_OR_CONSUMER_OF_stableFileId_IN_SCRIPTS_OR_SRC', re-confirmed unchanged), so this is a green-field single-owner design, not a migration away from a second owner.

lifecycleRules.MODIFY: same stableFileId; a new atlas_stable_file_revision_binding row with the new sourceRevision
lifecycleRules.RENAME_MOVE_SAME_REPOSITORY: same stableFileId; a new atlas_stable_file_alias row for the old path + an updated/new binding for the new path
lifecycleRules.DELETE: tombstone the stableFileId (lifecycle_state = TOMBSTONED); no row removed
lifecycleRules.RECREATE_SAME_PATH: a NEW stableFileId, unless continuity is explicitly proven by a separate lifecycle event -- never inferred from path/content/treeNodeId/packetId/graphify-file-uuid/git-commit alone
lifecycleRules.SAME_RELATIVE_PATH_DIFFERENT_REPOSITORY: a DISTINCT stableFileId, enforced structurally by the schema (bindings are scoped through stable_file_id -> repository_id, path uniqueness is never global)

unresolvedDecisions: Whether atlas_source_aliases is literally repurposed (add a stable_file_id column, widen its scope) for StableFileAliasV1, or a wholly new atlas_stable_file_alias table is created as proposed above. This design recommends the NEW table, because atlas_source_aliases's existing entity model (alias-of-a-source-ref, resolution_kind/status fields) is about resolving one path string to another canonical path string, not about binding a path to an opaque logical identity across a lifecycle -- a genuinely different entity, not a shape variation of the same one.

Whether repositoryId should be derived deterministically via the existing UUIDv8 utility (sveltekit-frontend/src/lib/utils/uuid.ts) keyed on {domainClass: 'atlas.repository-identity.v1', attributes: {gitmoduleName}} -- which would make repositoryId reproducible/idempotent by construction and arguably safer against the concurrent-create race in test F -- versus minted fresh via UUIDv7 with coordinates recorded only as attributes. Both are RFC 9562-compliant; this design leans toward UUIDv7 per the design gate's stated preference for stableFileId and treats this as an open question specifically for RepositoryIdentityV1, since a repository's identity (unlike a file's) has an unambiguous, stable, non-renaming name (the .gitmodules key) that a deterministic derivation could safely key on without violating the 'no path-derived stable id' rule (a gitmodule NAME is not a mutable file path).

Whether the 24,456 root-repository population A rows should be bulk-classified as SAFE_NEW_ID candidates now (as a read-only preview) or deferred entirely until S01-08J. This design defers it -- classifying at S01-08G risk pre-committing to a population count before the schema and canonical creator exist to validate against.
